data.name: Hezron
data.gender_notes: Hezron is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In the Hebrew Bible, Hezron is the name of Judah's second son. Hezron is also mentioned as the ancestor of King David. In Jewish tradition, Hezron is considered a righteous and worthy man. The name Hezron carries the meaning “Judah's son” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Hezron usually hope their child will grow to embody judah's son and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name representing strong lineage and ancestry in the faith.
data.etymology: Hezron belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Judah's son.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hezron total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: הזרון
in_hebrew.meaning: חיבור, קשר, או שושלת שמוצאה מאב מסוים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: הזרון הוא שם שמקורו בתנ"ך, ומשמעותו חיבור, קשר, או שושלת שמוצאה מאב מסוים. הוא שם שיכול להתייחס לקשר המשפחתי או הרוחני בין הדורות. בהקשר המקראי, הוא מוזכר כאביו של רם, ועל כן הוא חלק משושלתו של המלך דוד.

in_greek.name: Ἑζρών
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἑζρών ἐστιν ὄνομα προερχόμενο ἐκ τῆς Ἑβραϊκῆς γλώσσης, σημαίνων ἕνωσις ἤ σύνδεσμος ἤ γενεαλογία. Εἰς τὸν βιβλικὸν συμφραζόμενον, ὁ Ἑζρών ἐذكείται ὡς πατὴρ τοῦ Ραμ, καὶ ἕνεκεν τούτου, μέρος τῆς γενεαλογίας τοῦ βασιλέως Δαυίδ.

in_latin.name: Hezron
in_latin.long_meaning: Hezron is a name derived from Hebrew, signifying union, bond, or genealogical line. In biblical context, Hezron is noted as the father of Ram, thus being part of the lineage of King David. This name holds importance in Christian tradition due to its appearance in biblical genealogies.

in_english.name: Hezron
in_english.long_meaning: Hezron, originating from Hebrew roots, signifies a connection, bond, or ancestral line. Biblically, Hezron is mentioned as the father of Ram (Rahab), placing him in the lineage leading to King David and ultimately to Jesus Christ. This name carries spiritual significance in Christian tradition as part of the biblical genealogical records.

data.cultural_impact: Hezron holds significant cultural impact in Judaism and Christianity, as he is a prominent figure in both religions' ancestral lineages. In Jewish tradition, Hezron is recognized as a significant forefather, and his lineage is celebrated as a source of national pride and identity. In Christian tradition, he is also celebrated as a forefather of King David and, by extension, of Jesus Christ.
data.spiritual_significance: Hezron is also revered in both Judaism and Christianity for his righteousness and worthiness. In the Hebrew Bible, Hezron is mentioned as a man of great strength, as evidenced by his status as a forefather of both Judah and the future Davidic line. In Jewish tradition, this strength is interpreted as a spiritual one, representing the resilience and continuity of the Jewish people. In Christian tradition, Hezron's spiritual significance is amplified due to his place in the lineage of King David and, ultimately, Jesus Christ. Overall, Hezron's spiritual significance is rooted in his position as a righteous and strong ancestor, who serves as a reminder of the enduring covenant between God and his people.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Hezron, meaning "fortress" or "stronghold," represents the spiritual strength and protection found in God. As a Christian name, it serves as a constant reminder to embrace the fortified foundation of faith.

biblical_reference.note: Hezron is mentioned in the genealogical lists connecting Boaz to King David.

historical_references.reference: Hezron is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus in Matthew 1:5-6 as the father of Ram, who is the father of Jesse, who is the father of King David.
historical_references.context: Old Testament, Hebrew Bible, Book of Genesis and the New Testament, Book of Matthew.

historical_references.reference: Hezron is also mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2:13 as the father of Jerahmeel, the founder of the powerful clan of the sons of Hezron.
historical_references.context: Old Testament, Hebrew Bible, Book of Chronicles.

modern_usage.modern_context: Hezron is a biblical name mentioned in the Old Testament as the father of Jerahmeel, who is a forefather of King David. This name has gained popularity in modern times due to its rich historical context and the growing interest in genealogy and Bible study. On genealogy websites such as Ancestry.com, MyHeritage.com, and FamilySearch.org, Hezron is often searched for and used as a personal name by individuals tracing their family history. The name has also been adopted as a given name in some modern cultures, reflecting a trend towards using historical and traditional names for children.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named David Hezron in Jerusalem, Israel credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Hezron, which means "Judah's son". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
